== Sisters, Secrets, and the Morning Orion Vanished ==
After finishing an arm workout, [[Dalia Carter|Dalia]] collapsed onto her bed, muscles burning as she waited for the rain to stop so she could go jogging. [[Penelope Carter|Penny]] burst in soon after, cold and annoyed by the open window. Dalia apologized, explaining the gym was closed for the holiday and she did not want the room to smell. Penny teased her obsession with training but admitted Dalia’s progress was obvious, briefly easing the mood. She then noticed Dalia’s new hair, which Dalia said she had done the day before and forgotten about.
[[File:Penny and Dalia in Dalia's Room.png|thumb|Penny and Dalia in Dalia's Room]]
When Penny suggested they shower together like they used to, Dalia shut it down, clearly uncomfortable. Penny kept teasing until Dalia blurted out that she loved her just to make it stop. Laughing it off, Penny shifted to Eternum, asking about the recent mission. Dalia explained they had discovered [[Hassan Al-Rashid|Hassan]]’s incubation labs, where Xenomorphs were created through sacrifices, and planned to report it so the WRE could wipe everything out. With the secret exposed, she felt confident they would win the event and claim the [[Gem of Doom]]. 

Sensing something off, Penny pressed Dalia about a crush. Dalia denied it until Penny jokingly named Orion, and Dalia’s reaction gave her away. Cornered, Dalia admitted she and Orion had grown close through shared interests and time together. The moment exploded when Penny revealed she had been involved with Orion long before, turning the conversation into a bitter argument fueled by jealousy and old resentment.

They finally agreed the only solution was to confront Orion and force him to choose. They rushed through the house calling for him, only to find his room empty. [[Nancy Carter|Nancy]] appeared, confused, and reminded them it was a holiday. She admitted she was not even sure Orion had come home the night before, which was unusual.
[[File:Dalia and Penny cant find Orion.png|thumb|Dalia and Penny cant find Orion]]
Assuming he was with friends or stuck in Eternum, the sisters split up to look for him, still snapping at each other. Nancy watched them leave, coffee in hand, already exhausted and wondering how she was going to clean up whatever had just exploded between her daughters.

== Orion in the Hyril’ar Dungeon ==
A steady thud echoed as Orion’s fist struck the cold stone wall. His powers—teleportation, berserk strength—were gone, leaving him cut off and frustrated. Days in the dungeon blurred without sunlight.

Nearby, elven guards joked about rats and the Princess’s return. Their crude admiration made Orion tense; their tone was nothing like [[Calypso]]’s. From their chatter, he learned she had been recovered and might prevent war.
[[File:Orion in the Dungeon .png|thumb|Orion in the Dungeon  ]]
Desperate, Orion asked about Calypso. The guards responded with hostility, confirming she was alive but unconscious, blaming him. His denials meant nothing. Left alone, he sank to the floor as the guards reminisced about a human imprisoned centuries ago—until [[Regent Sylax]] arrived. 

Sylax entered with disdain, questioning Orion’s origins and connection to the Princess. He dismissed Orion’s protests and informed him that his trial before the Council awaited. Dumping a sack on the floor, Sylax ordered him to eat and change, mocking his pride when he refused.

Alone, Orion focused. This trial was dangerous, but it was also his only chance. Changing into ornate elven robes, he was shackled and escorted out, grateful for the sunlight by the lake.

Inside the Council hall, [[General Arannis]]’s cold indifference unsettled him. [[Regent Elenwen]] argued over [[Thorund’s Daughter]]’s presence until [[Regent Thorund]] confirmed she had been summoned as his successor.

Summoned forward, Orion tried to speak, insisting he had not harmed the Princess, but Thorund silenced him. He was charged with trespassing sacred land, violating ancient law, and laying hands on the Princess, who had been found near death in his presence. With no human entering [[Hyril'ar]] for centuries, the case threatened the Realm’s stability.

The trial began in secrecy, and Orion realized survival depended on answering carefully and speaking only when asked.

== The Trial ==
(For the following, Orion has three optional responses per question. For my own sake, only the recommended choices will be stated.)
[[File:The Council .png|thumb|The Council ]]
Orion began by asking who they were. Thorund introduced himself as the eldest noble of the Realm, Elenwen as the heir of Eldunar, and Sylax as the heir of Cassyr and King’s Hand. They collectively governed Hyril’ar in the Princess Calypso’s absence. Orion was shocked to learn she had vanished fifteen years ago, long before [[Ulysses]] even existed. Thorund instructed him to answer truthfully, warning that any deception would result in immediate execution. 

Orion explained he was the Princess’s sworn protector, having rescued her from the Immortals who held her captive. Elenwen and Sylax doubted him, claiming no human could serve her and that touching her was strictly forbidden by law. Orion insisted he had been genuinely useful and capable, proving himself in combat and in care for the Princess.

Thorund pressed Orion for proof of his loyalty, asking about Hyril’ar’s history. Orion correctly answered questions about [[Anima the Radiant|Queen Anima]], Yliar the Usurper, Calypso’s father Raewyn, her age, and the Elarisil ritual. Thorund nodded, accepting his knowledge as evidence. Thorund’s Daughter then explained the Sirfalas’kadhiel, an ancient trial by sparrow where fate would signal Orion’s innocence or guilt. Orion agreed, allowing the sparrow to choose, leaving the result to the omen.
[[File:Lorelei Testifies .png|thumb|Lorelei Testifies ]]
Before the verdict, Orion requested a witness: [[Lorelei]], General Arannis’ daughter, who had found him with the Princess in the forest. She confirmed his actions were benevolent and his intentions pure. Sylax protested, but Arannis reminded him that Lorelei was noble and one of the Princess’s royal maids. The Council allowed her testimony, after which Orion returned to the tense wait for judgment. 

The Council cast their votes. Sylax and Elenwen found Orion guilty. Thorund, however, declared him not guilty, delaying the final decision until further deliberation. Orion exhaled in relief as the guards returned him to his cell under strict watch. Thorund warned him that this reprieve was not weakness and that the new vote would come after reflection.

== Lorelei's Plan ==
Back in his cell, Orion sank against the cold stone wall, dread settling in. He hated the thought of spending Christmas locked away and felt helpless without his powers. More than anything, he wished he could let the girls know where he was.

A small rat squeezed through the bars. Orion greeted it absently, joking and offering scraps of food—until it transformed into Lorelei. Shocked, he barely reacted before she silenced him, warning her presence was dangerous.

Relief came when she admitted she’d come to help—but escape was impossible without months of advanced magic training. Her real reason: curiosity and a warning. The Council had decided Orion would be executed in three days.

Orion panicked, arguing the Princess would never allow it, only to learn Calypso remained unconscious and dangerously ill. Guilt crushed him. Lorelei explained the Princess’s isolation under strict rules. Orion clung to hope, but admitted that if Calypso didn’t wake soon, it might already be too late.

Lorelei offered alternatives: convince her father to exile Orion for decades, or use a forbidden remedy hidden in the forest that might wake the Princess, though the cost would be severe if discovered.

Doubting herself, Lorelei asked if Orion could be trusted. He swore his innocence and devotion to Calypso. After a long pause, she chose to trust him, promising to return within three days.
[[File:Rat-Lorelei waving Goodbye.png|thumb|Rat-Lorelei waving Goodbye]]
Their conversation was cut short by a guard. Lorelei transformed back into a rat just in time. Orion feigned harmless muttering until the guard left. Alone again, he sank to the floor. Three days stretched ahead like an eternity, and all he could do was think of the girls. 

== No Sign of Orion ==
In [[Ekabar]], the search for Orion led the group back to the inn, the last place anyone had seen him. The innkeeper, startled during his morning routine, quickly found himself cornered by [[Alex Bardot|Alex]], who accused him of hiding Orion and Calypso. Despite the threats, the man swore he knew nothing, insisting that after Orion left, half the inn room had burned down and both he and the elf had vanished without a trace. Nancy stepped in to calm things down, reminding Alex that they had already questioned him and that he lacked the power to pull off anything serious. Reluctantly, Alex backed off, though her frustration was clear.

Outside, Nancy reassured Alex that they would find him. Alex admitted her anger came from anxiety, apologizing for losing her temper. Nancy reminded her that Eternum was massive and that five days, while stressful, did not mean the worst. Penny soon returned from questioning the villagers, exhausted and discouraged. No one had seen Orion or Calypso, and the lack of answers was starting to wear on her. Nancy refused to let Penny spiral, insisting that whatever had happened, they were together and alive, even suggesting they could be trapped in a long dungeon or had somehow returned to Hyril’ar.
[[File:Dalia in after looking for Orion in Ekabar.png|thumb|Dalia after looking for Orion in Ekabar]]
Dalia soon joined them after checking the mill. While rumors about the miller being involved in shady dealings proved true, it turned out to be nothing more than drug smuggling, with no sign of Orion or Calypso. Her battered armor raised concern, but she brushed it off, explaining it was old damage and a brief scuffle with the miller’s hired help. Despite insisting she was fine, Dalia made it clear that whoever was responsible for Orion’s disappearance would regret it.  

The group’s attention shifted when Alex spotted smoke rising from Jebediah’s house, one of the first people to see the aftermath from the inn incident. Seeing it as their first real lead, they rushed off together, tension thick in the air. As they moved, Penny and Dalia exchanged sharp looks without speaking, their unresolved conflict hanging between them.

Left briefly alone, Nancy quietly pleaded for Orion to show up soon, knowing that in just five days, the group was already starting to fracture under the strain of his absence.

== Between Sleep and Stone ==
[[File:Idriel appears in the cell.png|thumb|Idriel appears in the cell]]
Orion slowly opened his eyes, groaning as a sharp headache tore through his skull. Sleeping on the cold, wet stones without a pillow had done nothing to help, and he felt every nerve screaming in protest. His head felt like it was about to split open, and he briefly considered asking the guards for a painkiller, though he knew it would be useless. As he tried to gather his thoughts, a strange presence filled his mind, and he immediately recognized it—[[Idriel]]. Panic surged through him; he didn’t want to see or hear anything from this entity. Idriel’s voice questioned the nature of reality, asking whether something is real if it can be felt, even in dreams, memories, or fear. Orion refused to engage, insisting he didn’t care and demanding the voice leave. 

Idriel laughed softly, insisting they weren’t so different, bound by the same chain. Orion recalled the times he had seen Idriel before—when he was shot in an alley and again when [[Thanatos]] nearly killed him at the inn—and wondered why these visions kept haunting him without offering any answers. Idriel offered a story, and despite Orion’s resistance, he reluctantly agreed to listen.

The story described an ancient door, worn smooth by countless hands, and a man who stood before it, knocking repeatedly. The door remained shut despite his efforts, and the man turned to leave, only to be urged to try once more. On this final attempt, the door finally opened. Orion understood that something had changed in the man himself, not the door, though Idriel remained enigmatic about the specifics. When Orion asked what was behind the door, Idriel only said it was a good question, leaving the answer unspoken. Just then, a knock at Orion’s cell door pulled him out of the lingering dream, jolting him back to the cold reality of the dungeon.

== The Princess Intervenes ==
The guard barked that Orion had been summoned. He got up reluctantly, hoping this might be his chance to defend himself without Lorelei. Changing clothes was unnecessary.
[[File:Orion about to be Hanged.png|thumb|Orion about to be hanged ]]
Escorted by General Arannis and the guards, he was led toward a nearby canyon. He tried to silently plead that the Princess would understand once she woke. Before he could react, two guards grabbed him and dragged him to the noose. The sentence was pronounced: for crimes against Hyril’ar and the Princess, he was to be executed. Orion protested, insisting he was innocent, but the guards cited the law as Regent Sylax and Regent Thorund watched. 
[[File:Calypso stops the execution.png|thumb|Calypso stops the execution]]
His mind raced. Lorelei had said he had three days, yet he now faced death. Struggling against the rope, he prepared to activate his powers. Just as execution seemed inevitable, everything changed. The guards paused. Princess Calypso appeared, commanding attention. The regents bowed in surprise. 

She declared Orion had saved her life and that the others’ judgment had been wrong. The execution was canceled. Instead, he would serve as her personal bodyguard until her recovery. The regents complied, and the guards untied him. Orion exhaled, shaken but alive, another near-death experience behind him.

As preparations for travel began, he noted the organized chaos: sacks loaded, horses saddled, guards briefing. They were retreating to the Usurper’s fortress at the Princess’ command. Orion wouldn’t see her until arrival, but he found comfort knowing she was awake. Twelve hours of carriage lay ahead, surrounded by wary guards, but it was better than the dungeon. He sighed, trusting the girls were safe and capable while he waited.

== Trying to find Clues in the Chaos ==
[[Sandra Johnson|Sandra]] knocked gently on [[Nova Johnson|Nova]]’s door, then again, growing more insistent as there was no response. Inside, Nova was half lost in thought, muttering to herself while scribbling and staring at her screen, completely absorbed in patterns, numbers, and theories that refused to line up. Sandra sighed, called her name louder, and finally mentioned that [[Annie Winters|Annie]] was there to see her. That snapped Nova out of her spiral just enough to recognize the name. She told Sandra to let Annie in, already drifting back into her thoughts as Sandra stepped away, quietly hoping the visit might help lift Nova’s mood after the last few days. 
[[File:Annie has a depressing aura.png|thumb|Annie has a depressing aura]]
In the hallway, Sandra tried to make polite conversation with Annie, worried about Orion. She suggested he might be visiting family or lost in Eternum, but Annie shut that down—Orion had no family, and Eternum was dangerous. Sandra, out of her depth, offered to let the police handle it, unaware that Eternum’s rules made that impossible, and then left for Nova’s room.

Inside, Annie apologized for being late, exhausted. Nova barely registered it, fixated on a realization about dates and formats. She announced she had cracked everything and claimed to know exactly where Orion was. Her explanation spiraled wildly, covering ciphers, conspiracies, Calypso, Ulysses, and Eternum’s core server, eventually pointing to Central Africa. Annie struggled to keep up, questioning whether Nova had slept at all.
[[File:Nova and her Board.png|thumb|Nova and her Board]]
When Nova insisted they needed to travel to Africa, Annie broke down. She admitted she didn’t believe Orion was there and confessed she had no idea where he was. Overwhelmed, she voiced her fear that he might be gone for good. Nova, frustrated but determined, pressed on with logic and hacking plans, refusing to give up. 

[[Luna Hernandez|Luna]]’s calm voice finally grounded them. She said with certainty that Orion was okay and would return, trusting his strength and that he would never abandon them. Slowly, tension eased. Annie wiped her tears, acknowledging Luna was right, and Nova forced a laugh, embarrassed by her spiral. They shared a small laugh, grateful for Luna’s steadiness.

Nova snapped back into energy, insisting it was time to regroup and approach the search with clearer heads. They scrapped the Africa theory and brainstormed new possibilities, including that Orion could be held by ERE remnants on another server. For the first time in days, panic gave way to a plan.

== Hope Rekindled in Hyril'ar ==
Orion lay half-awake in the sleeping quarters, frustrated by how little control he still had over his transformation. His powers were slowly returning, but he couldn’t hold them for more than a second, leaving him sore, exhausted, and irritated. Daily training was taking its toll, and his body still ached from the previous sparring session. When the general arrived to summon him, Orion groaned at the thought of more drills, briefly wishing he had never insisted on such a relentless schedule.
[[File:Orion hugs Calypso.png|thumb|Orion hugs Calypso ]]
Then, the Princess appeared, and Orion, overwhelmed with relief at seeing her alive, rushed forward and pulled her into a tight hug. Calypso, initially shocked, eventually returned the embrace before pushing him gently away as the general cleared his throat. She reminded him how dangerous such behavior was in a place like this, especially given his state of undress, and Orion apologized, explaining that he had been so surprised to see her that he’d forgotten where he was. 

With the general dismissed for the moment, the Princess explained that she had arranged to accompany Orion during his training so he could finally ask the questions that had been brushed aside. She clarified their location within Hyril’ar, describing the vastness of the kingdom and their journey from the border regions to Iskhaldrim, a fortified settlement nestled deep in the mountains. Orion listened with mild disbelief, joking internally about never remembering all the names, while quietly marveling at how expansive the realm truly was.

Concerned, Orion asked about her condition, relieved to learn that she was steadily recovering after exhausting herself in battle. She recounted waking to the news of his impending execution and regaining her strength just in time to intervene. Hearing this, Orion admitted that he too had been growing stronger since that day, privately wondering if their powers were somehow linked. When he finally asked how he could return to Earth, she revealed that she believed she could open a portal the following day, though not directly to his world. The news filled Orion with renewed hope, as any Eternum server would be enough for him to find his way back.

They spoke briefly of Lorelei, whose forbidden knowledge had saved the Princess’s life and earned her a royal pardon. Orion felt grateful, knowing he owed her more than he could repay. As their conversation drew to a close, the Princess suggested they part ways before training, explaining that being seen alone with a human still carried risks, no matter the truth. She admitted that her own views on humans had once been harsh, but that knowing Orion had changed her perspective.

Left alone, Orion watched her go, his spirits lifted for the first time in days. She was safe, his strength was returning, and for the first time since arriving in Hyril’ar, there was a clear path forward. Tomorrow, he might finally leave this place and reunite with the girls. All he had to do now was survive one more day and not ruin everything before then.

== Training Session ==
[[File:Arannis and Lorelei.png|thumb|Arannis and Lorelei]]
Orion paused at the crossroads to take in the sweeping valley, struck once again by its quiet beauty and how unreal it felt, even after days of staring at it. As he continued on, he soon encountered General Arannis and Lady Lorelei, thanking them for escorting Calypso earlier and expressing how her presence had lifted his spirits. General Arannis, stern as ever, made it clear that while he would respect Calypso’s wishes, Orion’s role came with strict boundaries and grave consequences should he ever overstep them. Orion accepted the warning without hesitation. 

Calypso and Lorelei soon joined them, exchanging warm pleasantries that showed their long shared history. General Arannis voiced concern about Calypso’s striking appearance being a liability, but she dismissed it, confident in the valley’s seclusion and her own abilities. As they walked, the emptiness of the valley became apparent, prompting an explanation that the people and soldiers had been relocated due to growing tensions and declining birthrates. Calypso accepted this grim reality with resolve, already thinking ahead to what she would need to repair once fully recovered.
[[File:The big Gates.png|thumb|The Massive Doors]]
Their path led them to an ancient hidden temple, older than elves or humans, where Orion noticed a familiar symbol carved into the massive doors: [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ouroboros the Ouroboros]. The realization that a symbol from his own world existed here unsettled him deeply and raised troubling questions about ancient travelers and lost connections between worlds. Despite his curiosity, the sealed doors could not be opened, and the group instead prepared for training nearby. 
[[File:The start of Training.png|thumb|The start of Training]]
General Arannis pushed Orion harder than before, replacing wooden practice blades with real steel and showing no mercy in his approach. Fear and doubt surfaced briefly, but when pressed about what he would do to protect those he cared for, Orion found his resolve. Their clash was intense, ending with Orion’s blade poised at General Arannis’s throat. Though impressed, the general reminded him that real enemies would show no restraint and demanded even greater focus and speed. 

As training continued, Calypso and Lorelei observed from the sidelines, openly impressed by Orion’s strength, stamina, and rapid growth. Their conversation drifted into curiosity about humans and Orion’s companions, until Lorelei’s unchecked fascination crossed into awkward territory, earning a sharp rebuke from Calypso. The moment was cut short by news of a druid’s arrival, drawing Calypso away for urgent matters. She departed with composed grace, leaving Orion to refocus on his training under General Arannis’s watchful eye.

== The Druid's Warning ==
Calypso greeted [[Lady Briena]] in her chambers, struck by how little the ancient druid had changed despite the years. Briena reacted with open astonishment and reverence, treating Calypso’s return as nothing short of a miracle. Their exchange carried an easy familiarity, shaped by centuries of shared history and Briena’s blunt honesty, a trait Calypso herself had once encouraged.
[[File:Calypso and the Druid.png|thumb|Calypso and the Druid]]
The reason for Briena’s summons soon became clear. She had already anticipated Calypso’s concerns, having sensed the weakening of her magic through the letter sent from the capital. Briena offered her an herbal tea meant to ease the symptoms, explaining that while it would not cure the problem, it would provide temporary relief. Calypso accepted it and was surprised by its pleasant taste, allowing herself a brief moment of comfort before turning to the real issue. 

Calypso described the lingering emptiness she had felt since awakening from her imprisonment. Though physically unharmed, her magic had become sluggish and difficult to control, with even simple acts requiring great effort. Briena listened carefully and revealed that this was not the first time such an affliction had appeared in Calypso’s bloodline. She explained that Calypso’s magic was not fading, but deprived, likening it to deep roots starved of nourishment.

According to Briena, the power of Anima within Calypso was meant to be expressed rather than contained. Suppressing it for too long had caused instability, which now manifested as exhaustion and weakened spellcasting. Calypso needed sex. Though Calypso initially rejected the explanation as absurd and deeply insulting to her dignity, Briena insisted she spoke from knowledge, not superstition, clarifying that balance, not obligation or motherhood, was the core issue.

Briena then revealed that steps had already been taken to protect both Calypso and the realm. A Suitor’s Rite had been arranged at Usurper’s Keep, involving three carefully chosen candidates from powerful houses. The union would stabilize Calypso’s magic and secure fragile alliances at a time when rebellion and foreign threats loomed. Though angered by the decision being made without her consent, Calypso ultimately understood the political necessity.

With visible reluctance, she agreed to attend the rite at dawn and make the choice herself, knowing refusal would be seen as weakness and invite further unrest. Briena, satisfied but not unkind, took her leave to prepare the keep, leaving Calypso alone in silence, burdened by the weight of what lay ahead.

== Pushing Limits ==
[[File:Orion Pushing his Limits.png|thumb|Orion Pushing his Limits]]
Orion staggered under Arannis’s relentless commands, sweat burning his lungs as his footing slipped and his timing faltered. He cursed through ragged breaths, forcing himself upright and insisting he understood his mistake, begging for another chance. Arannis judged him plainly and called for rest, noting how each attempt slowed him further. Orion refused. He said he was leaving the next day and could not stop now, not while there was still light. When pressed on his stubbornness, he admitted the truth. He needed to be better. He could not fail again. Too much depended on him. Arannis studied him in silence, then smirked and allowed the training to continue. They pushed on until sunset, the commands sharper, the pace faster, Orion answering each with obedience and grit as he fought exhaustion itself. 

== Staying Behind ==
Orion slept deeply until distant thunder pulled him back to consciousness, the promise of a coming storm echoing through the keep. His body ached pleasantly from Arannis’s brutal training, hunger already gnawing at him as he dragged himself from bed. A knock came at the door, and Arannis informed him that the Princess wished to see him regarding a portal home. The realization hit at once. He was finally leaving. Scrambling to dress, he barely had time to complain about elven clothing before Calypso quietly appeared inside the room, catching him off guard.

Calypso explained that she had gathered enough strength to open a portal for him, yet something about her felt unsettled. Orion noticed immediately and pressed her gently, offering a space where she could speak freely without courtly masks or politics. She admitted that returning to Hyril’ar felt wrong in a way she could not explain. Everything was unchanged, frozen in time, while she herself felt diminished. Her magic no longer answered her as it once had, and the weight of expectation pressed down harder than ever. At last, she confessed the truth she rarely allowed herself to acknowledge. She did not want to be a princess. She wanted freedom, movement, risk, and a life shaped by choice rather than duty, much like the time she had spent traveling with him.
[[File:Calypso rests in Orion's arms.png|thumb|Calypso rests in Orion's arms]]
Orion asked permission before pulling her into a hug, trying to ground her the only way he knew how. After a brief hesitation, she allowed it, leaning into him and returning the embrace before slowly pushing him away, steadier than before. The comfort did not change her obligations, but it cleared her thoughts enough to speak of what awaited her. She revealed that she was expected to choose a husband that very day, a political union meant to stabilize the realm and, according to the druids, help restore balance to her magic. The news stunned Orion, and he bristled at how quickly everything moved, yet Calypso accepted it with weary resolve. 

The moment was broken by the distant toll of a bell, signaling the arrival of the suitors. Calypso prepared to leave, thanking Orion for the brief peace he had given her. She opened a portal for him to Ekabar, promising that once her affairs were settled, she would come to him herself. As Orion stepped toward the portal, doubt crept in. Something about leaving now felt wrong. Turning back, he chose instead to stay and accompany her to the keep, refusing to let her face the ordeal alone. He framed it simply. You stay for people because they matter.

Calypso accepted, flustered but relieved, insisting he at least finish dressing properly. Together, they left the chamber side by side, Calypso granting him the role of her protector as they walked toward whatever awaited them next, both aware that this chapter was far from over.

== The Suitors Arrive ==
Calypso leaned back and questioned Orion about the limits of what he could carry between Eternum and Earth. He explained that items from his world could come with him as long as he was holding them, but objects native to Eternum stayed behind. The Gems were the lone exception, always returning with him no matter where he appeared, for reasons he did not understand. Living beings could cross if he was touching them, though he admitted it was dangerously risky and something he never intended to repeat after bringing Nova, Dalia, and accidentally Alex. When Calypso asked if someone from Eternum could travel to Earth, Orion said he had tried once and failed. Artifacts and people bound to Eternum could not cross over.

Calypso admitted she had sometimes wondered what Earth might be like after hearing him speak of it so often, but dismissed the thought as fleeting. Her duty and life were rooted in Hyril’ar, whether she enjoyed ruling or not. Orion privately reflected that knowing how little she enjoyed her role only made him want to find a way to take her to Earth, even if he had no idea how.

Arannis entered the chamber and bowed, announcing that preparations were complete and the suitors were assembled. Calypso ordered their entry while keeping their delegations at the gates and instructed that most of the guard be assigned to greet them, projecting strength despite stretched forces. After Arannis departed, Orion asked about previous suitors. Calypso explained that Lord Thorund had pressed the issue since her parents’ deaths, but none had been worthy. A king of Hyril’ar had to come from an equal house and excel in battle and the three sacred arts. Orion jokingly measured himself against those standards, but Calypso made it clear that a human courting her would cause outrage and possibly war, though she teasingly allowed that sweet enough music might earn a passing thought.
[[File:Lorelei waves back at Orion.png|thumb|Lorelei waves back at Orion]]
As Calypso’s maids took their seats, Orion noticed Lorelei among them and waved, earning hushed surprise from her side and irritation from the opposite benches. The [[Court Chamberlain]] formally announced the arrival of three suitors and explained the traditions of presentation and deliberation. When the matter of appointing a champion arose, Calypso revealed that Arannis was unavailable and instead named Lord Orion as her champion. Shock rippled through the court, led by Regent Thorund’s outrage. Calypso ended the objections by ordering that Orion’s identity be concealed beneath a helm and declaring her decision final. The Chamberlain reluctantly complied, warning Orion to speak only when permitted and to avoid disgracing the court. 

The suitors were then summoned. [[Fael of Thirinvale]] entered first, graceful and eloquent, praising Calypso’s beauty and listing his ancient lineage and victories. [[Orym of Ilvenmyr]] followed, solemn and honorable, speaking of duty, valor, and the ancient bond between their houses. Finally, [[Torion of Reveil]] strode forward, imposing and blunt, promising powerful heirs and a realm forged in strength. Calypso acknowledged each in turn, maintaining her composure despite the contrast in approaches.
[[File:Sir Grothelborn.png|thumb|Sir Grothelborn]]
With the presentations complete, the Court Chamberlain announced the traditional trials. Orion, now known publicly as Sir Grothelborn of [[Kredon]], stepped forward as champion, feeling the weight of hostile stares but resolving not to fail Calypso. The court declared that the suitors would prove themselves in archery with a longbow, and demonstrations of poetry, painting, and music. As the signal to begin was given, Orion realized just how much more complicated the trials would be than he had expected. 

== The Elven Games ==
The Court Chamberlain announced the first trial of the noble arts: poetry. Each suitor, including the champion, was given one minute to compose a four line verse dedicated to Princess Calypso, with complete freedom over theme and structure. Orion struggled to even understand what was being asked as the first suitor, Fael of Thirinvale, stepped forward almost immediately and delivered a bold and provocative poem that drew a mix of admiration and surprise from the court. Calypso acknowledged it as daring yet poetic, with Regent Thorund openly praising its evocative nature.

Orym of Ilvenmyr followed, presenting a refined and elegant verse filled with imagery of nature and quiet reverence. His words were warmly received, earning sincere praise from both Calypso and the regents. Torion of Redveil came next, offering a harsh and violent poem centered on conquest and domination. While unsettling, parts of the court admired its raw intensity, and Calypso noted its visceral quality despite its brutality.

When Orion was finally called, the Chamberlain pressed him to either present or step aside. Orion moved forward anyway and delivered a simple, earnest poem focused on a small, sincere moment with Calypso. The court was divided, but Calypso openly stated that she liked it, surprising many and firmly halting any attempt to dismiss or destroy his work. With that, the Chamberlain declared the poetry trial concluded and announced the second noble art: painting.
[[File:Calypso and Lorelei talking.png|thumb|Calypso and Lorelei talking]]
Each participant was given an hour, a blank canvas, and fine paints. Orion struggled with doubt but ultimately chose to paint Calypso herself, using her presence as inspiration. As the painting continued, Calypso circulated the hall, clearly weary of the surrounding courtly chatter. During this time, she quietly confided in her maid Lorelei, expressing how deeply she disliked the endless ceremonies and how different things felt after spending time among humans. She admitted she missed the simplicity and honesty she had experienced with Orion, finding human interactions far more genuine than the calculated politeness of court life. Their conversation drifted into awkward curiosity and embarrassment before being cut short by the end of the painting trial.  

The Chamberlain and Calypso first examined Torion of Redveil’s work, a detailed depiction of his grandfather during an ancient war. Though skillful, it portrayed humans as monstrous figures, which Calypso quietly questioned before accepting the symbolic explanation. Orym of Ilvenmyr presented a highly accurate painting of Iskhaldrim, despite never having visited, earning strong praise for its precision. Fael of Thirinvale unveiled a confident self portrait depicting himself as a future king, a daring choice that impressed some and unsettled others.

When Orion’s painting was revealed, the Chamberlain openly mocked it as crude and childlike. Orion defended his effort, explaining he had never painted before. Calypso immediately intervened, declaring that she liked it and valued the intent behind it. She ordered that it not be destroyed and ended the debate, moving the court forward to the third noble art: music.

The Chamberlain announced that each suitor would perform an improvised piece on the lyre. Torion of Redveil performed first, stunning the court with an unexpectedly masterful and emotional melody. The performance was widely praised, including by Calypso herself. Orion followed last. Clearly outmatched, he gave an awkward and unconventional performance that shocked the court. While the Chamberlain reacted with outrage, Calypso defused the moment by calling it memorable and urging the court to move on.

The final trial was combat, conducted through a single archery shot using the same bow and arrow for all participants. Fael of Thirinvale struck near the inner ring, followed by an even better shot from Orym of Ilvenmyr. Torion of Redveil nearly hit the center, setting an intimidating standard.
[[File:Orion hits a bullseye .png|thumb|Orion hits a bullseye  ]]
Orion stepped forward last. Struggling with the unfamiliar weight of the bow, he steadied himself and focused, drawing on everything Arannis had taught him. His arrow struck the exact center of the target, even displacing Torion’s shot. The court was stunned. Calypso openly praised him, declaring that he had fully proven himself as the champion of Hyril’ar.  

With the trials concluded, the Chamberlain declared the day a celebration and ordered the feast to begin. As nobles gathered around Calypso and servants filled the hall, Orion quietly slipped away to the edge of the room.

== A Champion's Exit ==
Orion quietly accepted that his role in the trials was finished. He felt he had done what he needed to do, and at the very least, Calypso had seemed genuinely relieved to have him at her side throughout the ordeal. With the feast underway, he decided it was best to return to his chambers before any of the suitors noticed something was off and realized he was not actually an elf.

Before he could leave, Torion of Redveil approached him and addressed him as Sir Grothelborn. Orion turned to face him and explained, somewhat awkwardly, that he could not remain at the feast due to a vow never to remove his helm in public, one he claimed was sworn to his late wife. Torion accepted this without question and took a moment to commend Orion’s exceptional archery, noting how impressive the shot had been even while wearing such heavy armor. He admitted that his own chances with Calypso were slim compared to Fael of Thirinvale or Orym of Ilvenmyr, but still extended an open invitation to Redveil should Orion’s path ever lead him there. Orion thanked him, surprised by the sincerity, and listened as Torion added that if rumors of civil war proved true, Redveil would stand with the crown and honor its old alliances. After they parted ways, Orion was left unsettled by the mention of civil war.

As Orion turned to leave, the Court Chamberlain stopped him and explained that he carried a message from Princess Calypso. She would spend the next few hours entertaining the guests and speaking further with the suitors, but she intended to meet Orion later in his chambers to open a passage back to his homeland before the day ended. Orion agreed easily and admitted he was looking forward to going home. The Chamberlain dryly remarked that he, too, looked forward to Orion’s departure, then grudgingly acknowledged that while Orion’s painting had been dreadful and his music painful to endure, his poem had been passable and his archery unexpectedly impressive, if perhaps aided by luck. Orion accepted the backhanded praise with good humor, thanked him, and finally took his leave.

On his way out, Orion decided he would either take a short nap or put in some extra longbow practice. After everything that had happened, he figured there was never a bad time to train.

== After the Suitors ==
A few hours later, Calypso finally sank into her chair, drained now that the halls were empty. She admitted that she had never imagined conversation alone could be so exhausting. Lorelei agreed, remarking that it was always worse when the heart was not truly in the exchange. Calypso thanked her for staying close through every tedious moment, and Lorelei replied that she would have remained even without duty compelling her. Calypso teased her about royal privileges and the extra glasses of Rivanor wine, which Lorelei quickly denied, insisting she could just as easily have stayed as Arannis’s daughter. Amused, Calypso withdrew the jab and dismissed her for the day, explaining that what remained now rested solely on her. She had to choose one of the three suitors to become her husband and the future king of Hyril’ar.

When asked how the meetings had gone, Calypso described them as hollow and ceremonial. Lord Fael hid crude innuendo behind grand promises of pleasure, Lord Orym spoke stiffly of duty and ancient family ties, and Lord Torion sounded more like a commander addressing a war council, obsessed with strength, blood, and warriors. Lorelei observed that none of them seemed to have truly moved her and wondered why Calypso could not refuse them as she had before. Calypso explained that the situation was different now. Her advisors feared the kingdom stood on the brink of war, unrest worsened by her long absence, and rumors claimed some old Houses might soon turn against the crown. A marriage might be the only way to preserve unity, and perhaps it was a debt she owed after so many years away. 

Lorelei argued that Hyril’ar was still strong, and that Calypso herself could defeat armies if needed, but Calypso hesitated and turned to her magic. She revealed that the Grand Druid believed Anima’s power within her was becoming volatile, yearning to be passed on and weakening her. Physical intimacy, the Druid claimed, could anchor it once more. Though uncomfortable, Calypso admitted this was another reason a suitor had to be chosen. Pressed to speak freely, Lorelei cautiously suggested that the act itself might matter more than the ceremony, but Calypso rejected the idea outright, warning that elven courts thrived on whispers and that any such secret would be weaponized against her. She added that she had already tried to resolve the matter alone, only to find her mind blocked and herself unable to find release.

Lorelei then hesitantly raised another possibility, mentioning Orion. Calypso reacted sharply, reminding her that he was human and that such a thing would be a grave crime under both law and ancient commandment. Lorelei argued that Orion was a stranger to the court and that Calypso had grown fond of him, but Calypso countered with the fate of Lady Arwil, stripped of her name and exiled after being discovered with a human. When Lorelei suggested Arwil’s downfall had come from carelessness, Calypso cut her off, declaring she would not allow a human to touch her, that she could not. Lorelei apologized and clarified that she had not meant physical contact at all, only that Orion’s presence might ease Calypso’s troubled thoughts. Calypso demanded an explanation, and Lorelei could only insist that she would do anything for her. Calypso answered with a quiet, unreadable sound, and the room settled into uneasy silence.

== A Private Request ==
[[File:Calypso and Lorelei show up in Orion's Chambers.png|thumb|Calypso and Lorelei show up in Orion's Chambers]]
Orion sat near the fire, letting the warmth sink in as night settled over Hyril’ar. The cold always seemed sharper once the sun went down, and it left him wondering how this world even measured time. Seasons, months, days. Everything here still felt foreign, and it only reminded him how much he did not understand yet. He caught himself thinking that once the Gem War was over, he wanted to return properly with the girls and truly learn this place. The thought drifted into a half joking idea about whether being the head of Ulysses might earn him some kind of standing at court, before a knock pulled him out of it. 

Lorelei’s voice came from the door, followed by Calypso herself when Orion invited them in. They entered quickly and shut the door behind them. Orion froze for a moment, struck by Calypso’s appearance. Her night robes were far less formal than her usual attire, light and sheer in places, clearly chosen for comfort rather than ceremony. She explained that their discussions had run long and that she had changed after returning to her chambers, removing most of her jewelry while keeping her catalyst bracers. When she asked if it made him uncomfortable, Orion assured her it did not and even complimented her, earning a shy thanks in return.

Curious and a little anxious, Orion asked how things had gone with the suitors. Calypso admitted the conversations had gone smoothly enough but that she had felt no real connection with any of them. Orion hid his relief poorly, though he quickly thanked her instead for allowing him to stand by her side during the contest. Calypso told him his presence had brought her unexpected comfort, which was why she hesitated before admitting she needed one last favor before he returned home. She promised it would be the final thing she ever asked of him and that it would not take long.

As she paced the room, visibly nervous, Calypso stopped and made him swear that whatever she said would remain secret, for the sake of the entire realm. Orion agreed without hesitation, sensing the weight behind her words. She then began speaking carefully, explaining that while humans were known for strong impulses, elves shared the same desires but practiced far stricter discipline. Their low birth rate, she said, was not due to lack of desire but to biology, a consequence of their long lives. Orion struggled to follow where this was going, his thoughts racing ahead of reason.

Calypso cut herself off and returned to the real issue. Her magic, though stronger than when she first awoke after the battle with Thanatos, had become unstable over time. Simple spells still came easily, but greater ones now slipped from her grasp. The Grand Druid believed this imbalance came from unreleased inner energy, and that she needed to find release to restore harmony. When Orion finally understood what she meant, he panicked, only for Calypso to snap him back to attention and make it clear she was not proposing anything improper. No human would ever touch her, and she was already bending rules simply by standing before him as she was.

What she asked instead was far simpler. Alone, she could not focus long enough to reach the state she needed, her thoughts constantly drifting. Lorelei had suggested that visual assistance might help her concentrate. Orion slowly realized what that meant just as Calypso confirmed it. Lorelei, flustered and rambling, tried to justify the idea by insisting it was purely for the Princess’s sake and entirely academic, even as her own curiosity betrayed her. Orion stopped her, saying he understood.

Calypso reminded him that he was free to refuse, that this was not an order but a request made in trust, between equals bound by what they had already shared. Orion stood there in disbelief, stunned that such a moment was even real. In the end, he accepted. He told her simply that he would help, just as he always had.

Calypso laid back and undressed both Orion and Lorelei with her magic. Lorelei and Orion shared a romantic moment but Calypso was left unsatisfied. Lorelei was told to leave as Calypso said she reached release. Orion knew Calypso was lying and called her out. Orion convinced Calypso to help her and she gave in. In the end, thanks to Orion, Calypso was finally able to release. 

== Shattered Loyalty ==
A sharp knock rattled Orion’s door. Arannis demanded entry. Panic surged. Calypso froze, whispering in alarm, while Orion’s stomach dropped. There was no time to think. He urged her to hide; pride gave way to urgency. She ducked behind the bed just as Orion opened the door.

Arannis stormed in, scanning the chamber. Orion played the clueless outsider, claiming she had never arrived and he had been waiting for a portal home. Arannis cut him off, insisting Calypso was missing and must go to the Shrine of Lorithien unseen. Lorelei was already on her way. If she didn’t arrive by midnight, they were to flee without him. With that, Arannis left as abruptly as he came.
[[File:Calypso makes Orion swore to secrecy .png|thumb|Calypso makes Orion swear to secrecy ]]
Once the door closed, Calypso emerged, composed and ready. She agreed to go where Arannis instructed. Orion promised to deliver the message before returning to his world. Before parting, they shared a brief, private acknowledgment of what they had shared, swearing the secret would die with them. Calypso left, calling him her knight, leaving Orion rattled but determined. 

He searched the fortress. Corridors echoed with silence—no guards, no servants, kitchens abandoned. Instinct took over as an elven guard lunged from the shadows. Orion’s reflexive burst of power slammed the man to the ground. Recognizing him as one who had tried to string him up, Orion demanded answers. The guard cursed him, calling him a demon and boasting humans would be wiped from the continent, refusing to explain further. hi

Arannis entered, confirming Orion’s fears: parts of the Royal Guard had turned traitor, threatening Calypso. The Princess was already en route to the shrine, but the traitors might strike through someone she trusted.
[[File:Arannis aura farming and telling Orion to go without him.png|thumb|Arannis aura farming and telling Orion to go without him]]
Shouts echoed as more guards closed in. Arannis gave Orion a sword but quickly shifted orders. Lorelei mattered more than any stand here. Orion was to slip through the lines and reach Calypso, sending her to Vael’Thalas Hold. Orion hesitated, unwilling to leave Arannis, but was reminded that fighting wasn’t always about swinging a blade. Reluctantly, he obeyed. 

Unleashing his power, Orion vanished, racing toward Calypso. Confusion erupted among the soldiers as Arannis drew their attention. The standoff ended when Regent Sylax appeared, mocking Arannis and offering mercy in exchange for betrayal. Arannis refused, denouncing Sylax’s coup.

Sylax revealed the scope of his treachery: most of the Royal Guard had turned, cities pledged allegiance, and by dawn, a new banner would fly. Arannis warned of the doom this would bring, but Sylax spoke only of rebirth. Surrounded, Arannis stood firm, recounting his lifelong honor, the joy of Lorelei’s birth, and the trust of Calypso’s life. He admitted he never imagined his final stand would shield a human, but he would give his life to deny Sylax victory. As long as Calypso lived, Hyril’ar would never belong to him.

Sylax ordered Arannis’s execution. Surrounded and alone, Arannis remained unbowed.

== Between Duty and Desire ==
Orion staggered into the training grounds, soaked and gasping for air. This was where he had trained with Arannis on the first day, but now it was empty. Panic set in as he realized no one was there. He wondered if Calypso and Lorelei had escaped or been captured. He shouted Calypso’s name into the storm, but the thunder drowned him out. The ground had turned to sludge, the rain intensifying, frustration boiling over as he yelled again.
[[File:Orion fills Lorelei and Calypso in on whats happened .png|thumb|Orion fills Lorelei and Calypso in on whats happened ]]
Relief washed over him when Calypso answered from nearby shelter. She and Lorelei had realized the sound was not thunder. Calypso scolded him for standing in the rain and pulled him closer. Orion could barely catch his breath, overwhelmed that they were alive. Calypso urged him to change out of his soaked clothes, but he cut her off. There was no time. 

He told them everything. Hyril’ar was under attack from within. A coup. Sylax had turned much of the royal guard and launched coordinated strikes across the realm. Orion did not know how many had betrayed the crown, only that it was bad. Worse, they were coming for Calypso. She was the only thing in their way.

Calypso reeled, admitting she had been warned this might happen someday, just not now. Orion insisted they could not return to the palace. Lorelei argued that the guard answered to her father, Arannis, and he would never betray Calypso. Orion told her the truth. Arannis had been betrayed. He was the one who ordered Orion to warn them and get them out. When the attack began, Arannis stayed behind to buy time.

Lorelei panicked for her father, but Orion reminded her that Arannis was too valuable to be executed outright and too strong to fall easily. If they were captured too, there would be no way to help him. Orion had promised to get them to safety.

The weight finally crushed Calypso. She collapsed, trembling, anger and disbelief spilling out in muttered curses. Orion watched her struggle, seeing her shaken in a way he never had before. She spoke of broken oaths, of traitors, of not knowing who to trust. Orion reminded her of Arannis’s faith in her, and told her he believed in her as well.

That steadied her. Calypso rose, reclaiming herself, declaring they would move immediately. She sent Lorelei to gather supplies. As Lorelei left, a portal opened behind them. Orion recognized it, suggesting Ekabar so they could regroup. Calypso stopped him. The portal was only for him. She refused to risk being trapped away from Hyril’ar again. She would not abandon her people.

Orion argued, but knew her resolve. He instead passed on Arannis’s guidance, directions to Vael’Thalas Hold and the families who would never betray the crown. Calypso listened, thanked him quietly, and told him to go. He refused. If she stayed, so would he. They would face this together.

The tension softened. Calypso admitted the burden was crushing, that her father had ruled for centuries without faltering while she nearly lost everything in less than a decade. Orion told her it was not her fault, that strength was often mistaken for luck or fate. She questioned why he cared so deeply. He told her her war became his the moment she became part of his life.

She admitted she would leave everything behind if she could, but she could not abandon Hyril’ar. Still, she thanked him for showing her another way to live. For warmth, laughter, and moments that made life feel real. She promised that when this was over, she would walk away from the crown and return to him.
[[File:Calypso kisses Orion.png|thumb|Calypso kisses Orion]]
She stepped forward and kissed him, deep and breathless, as if time stopped. When she pulled back, Orion tried to follow and realized he could not move. She had done this deliberately. Calm and almost playful, she spoke of broken taboos and consequences she no longer feared. She made him promise to not die on her. 

Before he could stop her, she sent him into the portal. Orion screamed her name as the light swallowed him.

== Returning Home ==
Orion steadies himself as the world settles back into place. Ekabar. He is back. As he stands, he realizes Calypso was right. His teleportation power has returned, and he can move through Eternum again.

But Hyril’ar is gone from his senses. The absence feels wrong, the same hollow disconnect he felt before, only now it is focused on that single realm. He exhales sharply, frustration creeping in. Calypso always did things her way.

At least one thing is clear. The Gems of Doom matter more than ever. [[The Founder]], [[William Bardot|Bardot]], even Thanatos would come for Hyril’ar and for Calypso’s power. Orion will not let that happen. He will pull her out of that life, no matter what.

For now, all he can do is wait and trust that she can endure what is coming. If anyone can, it is her. With that thought, he turns his focus homeward. He has been gone too long, and he can only hope time has not moved on without him.

Orion exhales as he steps back into Kredon, struck by how good it feels to be home. It feels like he has been gone forever, even though he knows that is not entirely true. His thoughts race ahead to everything he needs to explain and how impossible it feels to even know where to start. Beneath the relief sits a quiet worry that things might have gone badly while he was gone, mixed with a strange hope that they noticed his absence, but not enough to truly suffer because of it.
[[File:The Girls cant find Orion.png|thumb|The Girls cant find Orion]]
As he calls out and moves further inside, he realizes everyone is here. The house is quiet in a way that makes his nerves spike, until he hears voices and understands what he has walked into. They have been searching for him. They have been arguing about leads, about waiting, about how far to go to find him. Hearing his name spoken with fear and frustration makes his chest tighten. 

When he finally reveals himself, the shock is immediate and overwhelming. The silence breaks all at once as everyone rushes him, fear turning into relief and anger and tears all tangled together. They had been terrified. They had counted the hours. They had imagined the worst. Even the strongest among them had been close to breaking, and some already had. Seeing that pain makes it hit Orion all at once just how much his disappearance affected them.

Apologies spill out as he tries to explain, clumsy and rushed, but no one truly needs the details yet. What matters is that he is here. He listens as Nancy tell him what those days were like, how they held on, and how Luna in particular kept everyone standing when it felt impossible. The realization leaves him quiet and heavy with gratitude.

Before anything else, he is urged to go find her. He heads out immediately, moving through familiar streets with his thoughts spinning. Seeing her again stops him in his tracks. Relief turns into urgency as he reaches her and tries to explain everything at once, how he was trapped, powerless, unable to reach them, and how sorry he is for the pain it caused.
[[File:Luna breaks down as she hugs Orion.png|thumb|Luna breaks down as she hugs Orion]]
Luna barely manages to hold herself together. The moment finally cracks, and she breaks down in his arms, admitting how afraid she was and how she doubted even her own visions. Orion holds her tightly, understanding now just how much she carried alone, smiling for everyone else while quietly falling apart herself. 

He soothes her, letting her cry without restraint, telling her she never has to hide herself from him. As the weight finally eases, he admits how much it hurt to see her like that, how deeply he cares, and how much he missed her. Holding her there on the street, he promises her something simple and sincere: that he will never disappear like that again, and that he will never leave her to carry that kind of fear on her own.

== Chillin at the Cafe ==
[[File:Luna at the cafe with Orionlsdhf.png|thumb|Luna at the cafe with Orion]]
A few days later, Orion sits on a café terrace, scrolling through the news and checking the balance in his uWallet. Eternum fills nearly every headline, and he finds himself wondering whether people truly do not know what is happening or simply choose not to. Luna joins him after breakfast, and they spend a quiet moment enjoying the rare sunlight and easy conversation. As they get ready to leave, she mentions her family visiting for the holidays and jokingly explains how her [[Mr. Hernandez|Father]] and [[Hugo|Uncle]] almost went into full panic mode after thinking Orion had upset her, only for the whole thing to be cleared up once they realized she had just been emotional from seeing him again. It is awkward in hindsight, but also strangely comforting to know how fiercely they look out for her. 
[[File:Changs Aura as he enters the cafe.png|thumb|Changs Aura as he enters the cafe]]
After Luna heads off, Orion reflects on how much she held everyone together while he was gone, even when she was scared herself. He wants to do something special for her, something she genuinely deserves. Before he can leave, a sudden flash of light announces [[Chang Wong|Chang]]’s arrival. Chang is in high spirits, eager to share that things with [[Micaela Garcia|Micaela]] have become serious, and Orion is genuinely happy for him. 

Chang gives Orion a thoughtful Christmas gift, a custom-made party board game, and asks in return for a full update on their plans. Orion fills him in on everyone’s holiday whereabouts, the upcoming Ulysses Corp job, and the larger hunt for the remaining Gems of Doom. By the time Chang leaves, Orion feels steadier than he has in days. Even with everything escalating, it helps to know some things, like loyal friends and small moments of normalcy, are still firmly in place.

== Escaping Eternum for the Holidays ==
Orion hurried to the meeting spot where Nancy was waiting, worried he might be left behind. The thought of spending Christmas Eve alone crossed his mind, but seeing the group in matching outfits quickly lifted his spirits. He apologized for being late, explaining he’d stopped at a café to meet Chang, and Penny assured him it was fine. Nancy admitted she hadn’t prepared anything special this year, but Orion reminded her how much better this felt compared to last year’s lonely Christmas. The plan to spend the night in the mountains sounded perfect, and the group agreed it was a rare chance to unplug from Eternum. Orion noticed Nancy had packed his warmer clothes, since her outfit alone wouldn’t suffice for the mountaintop. He also revealed a custom board game Chang had given him, and everyone was excited to play it later.
[[File:Nancy convinces Alex to go .png|thumb|Nancy convinces Alex to go ]]
Alex arrived next, hesitant to join, but Nancy insisted she was family and had to come. With everyone finally ready, Nancy reminded them to use the restroom before the drive. Penny and Dalia joked and teased over their jackets and hairstyles, their playful banter hinting at a week-long tension. Orion noticed it and Nancy explained it was a normal cycle for them, advising him to act naturally and not intervene. With the last bag loaded, Orion slid into the passenger seat, ready for a memorable Christmas Eve in the mountains. 

Orion and the group finally arrived at the mountain lodge, and Penny was immediately enchanted. Snow blanketed the tall spruces surrounding the cozy wooden house, making it feel like a scene straight out of a Christmas movie. Orion couldn’t help but chuckle at Penny’s excitement, realizing she really loved Christmas. She explained how much this holiday meant to her, and even though gifts were skipped this year, she was thrilled they hadn’t skipped Christmas entirely. Orion admitted he’d never grown up feeling the magic of Christmas, but Penny promised to make all his future Christmases special. Alex, having dozed off for part of the ride, yawned and apologized for passing out, insisting she help with the luggage. Nancy reassured her that it was fine and explained that one bag was refrigerated with ingredients for dinner and kitchen tools, while the other contained Penny’s foldable Christmas tree—because even though they were busy, a tree was essential.
[[File:Dalia tries out the pool.png|thumb|Dalia tries out the pool]]
Dalia gasped at the massive pool with its forest views, and Alex realized why she had packed a bikini. The pool was warm, like a private onsen. Orion complimented the setup while Nancy read the host’s note, revealing the lodge was anti-surveillance and fully secure from Ulysses’ agents. Orion was slightly taken aback by the extreme precautions, but Penny understood why there was no data coverage. Nancy reminded everyone that this could be their last normal weekend before their missions escalated, enforcing a strict “no Eternum” rule—especially for Orion, who could enter without a neural implant. 

Task assignments began: Dalia would help in the kitchen and bake cookies, Penny would prepare the beds and fireplace, Alex would decorate the tree, and Orion was on lumberjack duty, responsible for chopping logs and getting the fire going. Orion accepted his role, shivering slightly as he grabbed his jacket, ready to play lumberjack and contribute to the festive preparations. The girls dispersed with excitement, and dinner was set for six, with Nancy insisting they stay hungry until then.

Orion focused on chopping firewood, counting each log as he worked and stopping once he was confident there were enough to keep the fire going all night. As he finished, he couldn’t help but notice how easily the axe split each log clean in half, realizing that it wasn’t just practice or technique. He had genuinely gotten much stronger. Satisfied with the work, he prepared to head back inside and considered checking if Nancy and Dalia needed help in the kitchen. Before he could move on, his phone buzzed, surprising him since there was supposed to be no signal. He realized he must have stepped just far enough beyond the perimeter to reconnect and saw a message from Annie, who was excited to show him that it was snowing in London. They exchanged a few lighthearted messages, joked about the sudden signal, and said goodbye before she logged off. Orion smiled to himself, thinking about how adorable she was and feeling glad he’d been able to reply at all. Just as he assumed the signal would drop again, an unknown number started calling his phone, leaving him unsure whether to ignore it as spam or answer before losing reception entirely.

== Axel's Warning ==
Orion answered the call and was immediately met with frustration from the person on the other end, who turned out to be Axel. Axel asked if he was with Alex and explained that he couldn’t reach her either. Orion confirmed they were together in the mountains and pointed out the lack of signal, pressing Axel on why he was calling now after weeks of silence. Axel then dropped the reason for the call, claiming his father had killed Benjamin. Orion was stunned and pushed back, insisting a Praetorian was responsible and that the Founder controlled them, not William. Axel countered by saying his father controlled enough of them and claimed to know what was being planned, though he refused to explain over the phone. He insisted they meet in person. After some back and forth about timing, they agreed on Thursday evening at the park by the station. Before hanging up, Axel warned Orion not to approach his father under any circumstances and to stay out of it until they talked, stressing how dangerous he was.

Once the call ended, Orion pocketed his phone, uneasy and deeply suspicious of Axel’s motives. He couldn’t shake the feeling that Axel might be lying or working for his father, though he admitted it might still be worth hearing him out. There was no chance he could mention their plans to dig through William’s office on Wednesday without talking to the others first, especially Alex. Pushing the thoughts aside, Orion turned his attention back to the task at hand and went to gather the firewood, determined not to be the reason the fire went out and ruined Dalia’s marshmallow plans.

== Orion and Penny ==
[[File:Why Penny became a girl scout.png|thumb|Why Penny became a girl scout ]]
Orion carried as many logs as he could manage, hauling them back to the house and dropping them by the door. Hunger gnawed at him, but the warmth from the fireplace immediately enveloped him as he stepped inside, and he finally began to feel the Christmas spirit. Penny greeted him, relieved he hadn’t left the mountain bare. Orion explained it had taken a while to find decent dry wood, joking about his expertise, and mentioned he’d been delayed by a phone call from Axel Bardot, who wanted to meet on Thursday. Penny agreed that talking to Alex first was a good idea, but they both decided the call could wait—tonight was a detox from Eternum. They admired the Christmas tree and the fire, with Orion impressed that Penny had built it herself using dry timber and steel knives, revealing she was a five-time Best Girl Scout winner. As Orion walked down the narrow corridor, he reflected on how perfectly the trip was going and how the rain, which he once hated, now felt magical. When he reached the bathroom, he found it occupied and waited, growing increasingly uncomfortable. While standing there, he noticed [[Noah and Raul|Noah]] nearby, surprisingly separated from [[Noah and Raul|Raul]], and speaking with a man he recognized from earlier. Curious, Orion listened as [[Giuseppe Bellini]] spoke at length about his childhood dog, Nero, describing its strength, loyalty, and eventual decline. He recounted how his father had put the dog down out of mercy and explained that love sometimes takes cruel forms for the sake of what comes next. The story clearly carried a deeper meaning, and when the man asked if Noah understood, Noah eventually agreed. After a moment of silence, Noah shook the man’s hand, seemingly accepting some kind of deal, along with the idea of stepping out of another person’s shadow. 

The moment was broken when another passenger snapped at Orion for blocking the tight corridor. Orion moved aside, annoyed by the hostility but determined not to let it ruin his mood. As the man stormed off, Orion shook it off, reminding himself that nothing was going to spoil the day, even as the need for the bathroom became increasingly urgent.

== Using her Power for Good ==
As the train crossed a bridge, Luna quietly watched the scenery until the [[Train Conductor]] announced a brief clearing in the rain and pointed out a perfect view of Mount Baker. Luna hurried into the corridor to look, leaning toward an open window in awe as the clouds parted. While she was distracted, an irritated passenger tried to force his way past her in the narrow space. Startled, Luna apologized as he shoved by, and the brief contact was enough to trigger one of her visions. In an instant, she saw that the man was named [[Rowan]], and the vision revealed his explosive anger and the abuse he inflicted on his wife, [[Tessa]]. When it ended, Rowan dismissed her reaction and walked away, leaving Luna shaken and frozen in place.

Orion returned from the bathroom moments later, relieved that the rain had eased, and suggested continuing the movie. When he noticed Luna had put her gloves back on, he immediately sensed something was wrong. After some hesitation, Luna explained that Rowan, the same man who had bumped into her in the corridor, had triggered a vision showing him hurting his wife. Orion was furious and worried but focused on supporting Luna, reminding her that her visions were not her fault. When Luna said the future she saw could not be changed, Orion pushed back, pointing out that her powers did not work on him and suggesting they might be able to intervene together. After thinking it through, Luna agreed to try scaring Rowan into stopping, using what she had seen and a quick disguise. When the train entered a long tunnel and the lights flickered, they set their plan in motion.
[[File:Luna in her disguise .png|thumb|Luna in her disguise ]]
In the darkness of the carriage, Rowan grew increasingly unsettled as strange sounds and flickering lights surrounded him. Luna appeared before him, transformed and unrecognizable, confronting him with details only he could know. Terrified, Rowan broke down and promised to leave his wife, sign the divorce papers, and never return. As the train exited the tunnel, Rowan fled in a panic, shoving past other passengers as he ran back to his seat. Orion and Luna slipped back into their cabin just in time, hiding the disguise as Luna realized it had worked. Overwhelmed with relief, she was amazed she had used her powers to protect someone, and Orion reassured her, proud and steady, reminding her that this part of her did not need to be hidden. 

Caught up in the moment, they grew close and shared a passionate kiss until the conductor cleared her throat, politely apologizing for the interruption and letting them know the next stop was only minutes away. She mentioned a nearby abandoned house with a spooky reputation and suggested it was the perfect chance for photos. Intrigued, Luna immediately wanted to go, thrilled by the idea of exploring something haunted. Orion admitted he had planned it as a surprise and warned her it was probably just an old house with a legend, though he agreed to check it out. Eager not to miss their chance, Luna insisted they leave as soon as the train stopped.

== Shelter from the Storm ==
Orion and Luna stepped off the train into the deserted rural station and followed a narrow path toward the old estate grounds, still flooded from recent rains. The house looked mysterious, and while Luna wished they had more time to explore, Orion was quietly relieved they did not. The isolation stood out to him, with nothing but the rail line and scattered, lonely houses stretching across the region. Nearby, another couple argued loudly about pictures and wanting to leave, their bickering breaking the quiet.

Luna joked darkly about the murky water around the house, which made Orion pause before suggesting they take a picture. Luna immediately brightened, rushing to pose in front of the house with childlike excitement. Orion took a photo, struck by how she made even the creepiest place feel warm. Just as they talked about taking one together, the rain suddenly poured down. With no better option, they ran for the porch and slipped inside the abandoned house as the wind forced the door open behind them.

Inside, the cold set in fast. Orion searched for anything they could use to get back to the train while Luna tried to dry off, both half joking about ghosts. The house was mostly empty, filled with dust and rotting boards, though Orion managed to get an old generator running. He was surprised by how calm he felt, realizing that with Luna there, even a haunted house did not feel frightening.

In the basement, Orion found an old ceremonial mask and decided to try scaring Luna in playful revenge. His plan backfired when Luna used a trapdoor to sneak up behind him and scare him far worse than he intended. They both laughed hard, and Orion accepted that he would always be the one getting jumpscared, noticing how free and joyful Luna seemed.
[[File:Luna's reaction to hearing Orion say te amo.png|thumb|Luna's reaction to hearing Orion say te amo]]
When Luna worried she had been annoying and apologized for laughing so much, Orion reassured her, telling her there was nothing wrong with her and that being different was a good thing. Luna admitted she was still learning how to stop holding herself back now that she felt happier and more open. Orion told her she had changed for the better while still being the same kind, sweet, wonderfully strange person he cared about. Overcome, he told her how much she meant to him and  added ''te amo'', the words slipping out before he could overthink them. After a brief pause, Luna kissed him, ending his nervous doubt. 

They held each other quietly, the moment uninterrupted. Luna admitted she did not want to regret holding back, and Orion welcomed it, staying close as the rest of the world faded away around them. The two then share their third romance scene. 
[[File:Luna cute ah wave.png|thumb|Luna waves goodbye]]
Orion and Luna’s train ride back was filled with easy laughter and quiet moments, and soon they found themselves at the bus stop in Kredon. Orion couldn’t believe the day was already over, but reminded her it was only the first of many dates. Luna laughed, and the two shared a soft, sincere exchange of “I love you.”  

When the bus arrived, Luna assured him the ride home was short and promised to see him later in Eternum. She boarded, and Orion watched the bus disappear down the street. Alone, he thought about how perfect the day had been and how lucky he felt, then decided to head home, but not before heading to get some crepes. 

== Breaking News ==
When Orion finally got back home, he couldn’t stop thinking about how perfect the day had been. The time with Luna, the train ride, even dropping her off at her place all felt unreal. She felt unreal. He kicked off his shoes and called out to the empty house, hoping there was still food left because he was starving, only to notice a note instead. Everyone had gone out and planned to hop on Eternum later that night, though they hadn’t said which server. He considered crashing at Alex’s place or even bringing dessert as a surprise. With over an hour to spare, he told himself he should be productive, grab a snack, read a chapter, do some sit-ups, clean his room, then head out. As always, he reminded himself to squeeze every minute out of life.

He didn’t. Orion passed out on the couch almost immediately. When his phone buzzed, he woke up groggy and annoyed to see it was already past midnight. Another unknown number lit up the screen, and he assumed it was Annie, who had recently changed her phone after going to the UK. Half-asleep, he apologized for missing her calls and explained how he’d planned to surprise everyone but had fallen asleep instead. The voice on the other end told him to turn on the TV. That wasn’t Annie. The caller spoke in vague, unsettling phrases about an unavoidable moment, a Lady, and a path that had already been set, then repeated the demand to turn on the TV before hanging up.
[[File:Orion watching the news .png|thumb|Orion watching the news ]]
Uneasy, Orion stared at the remote, his thoughts racing. Weird things were normal in Eternum, but this was real life. After a few seconds, he turned on the television. The [[News Anchor]] was already calling it the worst technological failure in human history. Reports confirmed a catastrophic malfunction in the neural implant system. Players who died in the simulation or were forcibly disconnected were suffering instant fatal neural feedback in the real world. Ulysses executives blamed a cyberattack while critics accused them of criminal negligence. A global ban on implant usage had been issued, and viewers were warned not to disconnect anyone still logged into Eternum. As the anchor struggled to keep composure, preliminary casualty numbers were announced. The estimated death toll had already climbed past six hundred thousand.

As the Chapter ends, we see Orion, standing in front of the TV, drop his phone in shock.
